notes: failures.causes keys are condition flags the sim checks; values multiply the failure's weight. worn_part_slots match parts.json slots. damages_parts = slot:health lost.

outcomes.scrap: Print is binned. Filament up to the failure point is wasted. Printer is free after clearing (2 to 10 minutes of character time).
outcomes.stop: Printer stops and needs the fix before it can print again. Partial print is binned unless the printer has power loss or pause recovery.
outcomes.degraded: Print finishes but quality drops 1 to 2 stars. Sells for less, more returns and worse reviews. Player can choose to bin or sell it.
outcomes.shipping: Happens after sale. Triggers refund or replacement, review hit, and seller rating drop.

roll_rules.per_print_fail_chance: printer base_fail_chance_pct x preset fail_mult x material ease (6 - ease_of_printing) / 3 x product difficulty (0.6 + 0.2 x difficulty) + worn part extra fail % + wet filament bonus. Capped at 85%.
roll_rules.which_failure: If a failure is rolled, pick one weighted by base_weight x product of all active cause multipliers. Only failures valid for the printer type (resin, SLS, belt) are in the pool.
roll_rules.when: start = first 5% of print time, mid = random point 10% to 90%, end = shown on completion, post = after shipping or client inspection.
roll_rules.followups: Some failures raise the chance of others on the next print until fixed (e.g. bed_adhesion makes spaghetti and blob_of_doom more likely).
roll_rules.shipping_damage_chance: Per order: (5 - durability) x 2% x packaging multiplier x courier multiplier x size factor. Durability comes from the preset.

failures.name: First layer failed
failures.fix: Clean the plate and restart
failures.scene_visual: Squiggly half stuck lines on the bed
failures.sound: printer stops with a sad beep
failures.player_text: The first layer looks like a plate of noodles. Nothing else is going to stick to that.

failures.name: Print came loose
failures.fix: Clean with IPA, add a brim
failures.scene_visual: Part knocked over and dragged around the bed
failures.player_text: The print let go halfway and is now being pushed around like a hockey puck.

failures.name: Spaghetti monster
failures.fix: Clear the mess, find the cause
failures.scene_visual: Big nest of tangled filament where the print should be
failures.sound: none, which is the scary bit
failures.player_text: The printer has spent four hours knitting a bird's nest. Silently. Lovingly.

failures.name: Corners warped
failures.fix: Use an enclosure or a brim
failures.scene_visual: Corners lifted off the bed like a crisp
failures.player_text: The corners have curled up. It still sort of works, if your customer doesn't own a ruler.

failures.name: Layer shift
failures.fix: Tension or replace belts
failures.scene_visual: Print suddenly steps sideways halfway up
failures.player_text: Halfway up, the whole print decided to move one centimetre to the left. Bold choice.

failures.name: Nozzle clog
failures.fix: Cold pull or replace the nozzle
failures.scene_visual: Printer moving but nothing coming out, air printing
failures.player_text: The printer is very confidently printing nothing at all.

failures.name: Under extrusion
failures.fix: Replace worn parts or slow down
failures.scene_visual: Gappy, see-through walls
failures.player_text: Looks like it was printed by someone who was rationing plastic.

failures.name: Stringy mess
failures.fix: Dry the filament
failures.scene_visual: Fine cobweb strings between parts
failures.player_text: It's covered in fine little hairs. Seasonal for Halloween. Less so for a phone stand.

failures.name: Rough surface finish
failures.fix: Service the printer or use a finer preset
failures.scene_visual: Visible ripples and banding
failures.player_text: It works, but it has the texture of a cheese grater.

failures.name: Heat creep jam
failures.fix: Replace the hotend fan, clear the jam
failures.scene_visual: Filament mushroomed above the nozzle
failures.player_text: The plastic melted in the wrong place and set like concrete.

failures.name: Safety shutdown
failures.fix: Replace thermistor or heater cartridge
failures.scene_visual: Screen flashing a red warning, heaters off
failures.player_text: The printer noticed something was wrong with its own temperature and wisely stopped.

failures.name: Ran out of filament
failures.fix: Load a new spool and resume
failures.scene_visual: Empty spool spinning, print paused or abandoned
failures.player_text: Someone forgot to check the spool. Someone is you.

failures.name: Multicolour jam
failures.fix: Clear the jam in the multicolour unit
failures.scene_visual: Flashing light on the multicolour unit, filament stuck
failures.player_text: The colour unit has jammed and is flashing at you like it's your fault.

failures.name: Tangled spool
failures.fix: Untangle or bin the spool
failures.scene_visual: Filament snapped tight with a knot on the spool
failures.player_text: A knot formed somewhere deep in the spool. Nobody knows how. Nobody ever knows how.

failures.name: Supports collapsed
failures.fix: Turn supports on, or choose tree supports
failures.scene_visual: Overhangs drooping into strands
failures.player_text: The overhang had nothing to stand on and gave up.

failures.name: Blob of doom
failures.fix: Heat it up and carefully pick it apart, or replace the hotend
failures.scene_visual: Huge lump of plastic encasing the hotend
failures.player_text: The hotend is now inside a plastic boulder. This is the expensive one.

failures.name: Belt print slipped
failures.fix: Replace the conveyor or clean it
failures.scene_visual: Parts tumbling off the end of the belt early
failures.player_text: The belt printer launched your parts into the bin a bit early.

failures.name: Resin print stuck to FEP
failures.fix: Fish out the cured blob, replace FEP if punctured
failures.scene_visual: Half cured print stuck in the vat, empty build plate
failures.player_text: The print stayed in the vat instead of coming up with the plate. Fishing time.

failures.name: Dead screen pixels
failures.fix: Replace the LCD screen
failures.scene_visual: Holes or streaks in the same spot on every print
failures.player_text: Same tiny hole in every print. The screen is dying.

failures.name: Resin leak
failures.fix: Clean up, replace the FEP, check the screen
failures.scene_visual: Resin pooled under the vat
failures.player_text: There is resin where resin should never be.

failures.name: Short powder feed
failures.fix: Top up and sieve the powder
failures.scene_visual: Streaky, incomplete layers in the cake
failures.player_text: The machine ran short of powder. The parts inside are now a sad crumbly mystery.

failures.name: Power cut
failures.fix: Most printers can resume. Cheap ones can't.
failures.scene_visual: Lights out, printers dark
failures.player_text: The lights went out. Printers with power loss recovery can try to resume.

failures.name: Crushed in the post
failures.fix: Refund, replace, and use stronger prints or packaging
failures.scene_visual: Customer photo of a snapped item in a review
failures.player_text: It left your garage in one piece. It did not arrive in one piece.

failures.name: Failed client inspection
failures.fix: Reprint the rejected units before the deadline
failures.scene_visual: Rejected box returned with a red sticker
failures.player_text: The client measured everything. Some of it didn't measure up.
